title: observations
description: What one environment's hosts hold, as somebody collected it. A contract rather than a convention: it is what makes collecting and judging separable, so a closed network that has only Ansible produces this one file and carries it out to wherever review-sheet lives. Keys this tool does not read are allowed and ignored — a project's own channels (a product's API, a cloud API, the output of a command) live beside these.

environment.description: The environment column this stands for — the same name the sheets use.

collected_at.description: When, ISO 8601. Carried onto every evidence document, because two hosts' bytes were taken at two moments.

substitutions.description: What an importer's placeholders resolved to in this environment. Only the project read the files the importer read.

documents.description: Documents that belong to NO host. A `terraform plan` describes a cloud account, not a machine: which workstation ran the command is provenance of the fetch and not of the values. Filed here, a verdict citing one carries no host, its evidence label is what was ASKED, and the unit's "hosts checked" line never names a machine that has nothing to do with what the record certifies. Where the document sits is what says so — there is no flag.

name.description: What to call it, so a sheet can say which document answers its rows (`documents:` in the build spec).

sheet.description: …or which sheet's rows it answers directly, for a sheet whose rows carry their own addresses and need no template.

component.description: …narrowed to one component of that sheet.

format.description: How to read it. A realm comes back as JSON; nothing says another product's will.

how.description: What was asked, for the record's evidence — `GET /admin/realms/poc`. For a document belonging to no host this is the whole of its label, so it is what a reader sees beside every verdict it answers.

absent.description: …or it could not be read at all, which is an answer about the product and not a gap in the run.

probes.description: What a PROBE found for a check that belongs to NO host, keyed by the functional item's id. `terraform plan` run on a workstation or in CI answers "does the code still match the account", which is a fact about the account: no server was asked, and filing it under an invented one puts a fictional machine in the record's host line. Folded together with any host's probe for the same item rather than replacing it.

how.description: What was asked, for the record's evidence.

ran.description: Whether it ran at all. A probe that did not is a THIRD answer, never a failure.

why.description: …and why not, in the collector's own words.

ok.description: A verdict the collector itself could reach (an HTTP status is not a rule, it is the answer). Null where judging it needs one.

text.description: What came back, carried into the record as the material the verdict was read from.

hosts.description: One entry per host that was reached. A host nobody reached is absent, which is an answer.

files.description: Deployed path -> the bytes, or null for a file the host does not have. Null is an ANSWER, not a gap: every row of that file is reported not run, with that reason.

included_by.description: Which further files each deployed file NAMES. A row saying 'we set nothing, so the default applies' is a claim about those too.

formats.description: A format a path's own name cannot state (`space` is nobody's extension). Only where detection cannot serve.

probes.description: What a PROBE found, keyed by the functional item's id. A functional item has no row behind it, so what answers it is not a value at an address but whatever a probe produced — per host, because a fleet is only as configured as its least configured node.

how.description: What was asked, for the record's evidence.

ran.description: Whether it ran at all. A probe that did not is a THIRD answer, never a failure.

why.description: …and why not, in the collector's own words.

ok.description: A verdict the collector itself could reach (an HTTP status is not a rule, it is the answer). Null where judging it needs one.

text.description: What came back, carried into the record as the material the verdict was read from.

commands.description: What the host was asked, and what it said. One entry per command — the commands a CHANNEL asked for (`collect-plan` lists them), so the collector does not carry a second copy of the same strings.

documents.description: Documents the project fetched: a realm as a product's API describes it, a resource as a cloud API returns it. Not a file on this host and not a command's output — bytes that answer a whole sheet or component, addressed by each row's own structural address exactly as a file is.
